task.title: Reduce project load and cache-state resolution time
task.problem: Every run on freedesktop-sdk sdk.bst (615 elements) spends 24-28 s loading the project and resolving source cache state before any search; that is 75% of a warm-index find (32 s) and the floor for every query. A profile shows the dominant part is ElementSources.query_cache(): one casd FetchTree per element, which stats every file blob of the tree, issued serially.
task.proposal: Check each unique tree's completeness once, concurrently, with the same CASCache.contains_directory() call before Pass 1, and answer BuildStream's per-element query_cache() from those results; errors fall back to BuildStream's own call. A persistent element-to-digest cache is out of scope until the remaining load cost is measured.
acceptance: A load-phase profile on freedesktop-sdk identifies where the time goes.
Cache completeness is still verified with casd for every tree; failures surface exactly as before.
Load time on freedesktop-sdk sdk.bst drops measurably with identical results.
evidence: freedesktop-sdk sdk.bst (https://github.com/rmorozov/bst-utilities/actions/runs/37349192598): load 24-28 s -> 18.3-20.3 s. Locally with a warm page cache 8 workers cut the cache checks 1.43 -> 0.55 s. --stats now splits load into project load and cache check time to locate the remainder.

Review follow-up: cache checks are FetchTree futures awaited on the main thread and cancelled on interrupt (test_cache_checks_cancel_in_flight_rpcs_on_interrupt); remote-cache configurations keep BuildStream's own path.
